epic.intent:
Extend the FWGC++ procedural campaign (epic ep_01m4fpnf646t254mnh69jhz107) so the player picks one of the generator's peoples in Bannerlord's character creator, and the world is generated while the player is in the creator instead of before it.

User-confirmed scope (2026-10-15):

- **Every people gets its own selection.** All 12 FWGC++ civilizations are separate creator entries and replace the vanilla culture list for generated campaigns: human_heartland, human_maritime, human_desert, human_cold, human_large_island, human_rainforest, elf, tidekin, dwarf, hill_dwarf, frosthold_dwarf, gnome. Source: `kEntityIds` in FWGC++ `generator/src/generated/content_civilizations.cpp` at the `worldgen/producer.lock.json` commit; parent races (human, elf, dwarf) from `kParentRaces` and `generator/data/heritage-appearance.json`. The list does not depend on what the generated world contains.
- **Generation happens during character creation.** It starts when the creator opens and runs while the player works through the creator stages. The creator waits only at the end, if generation is still running, with progress, cancel and error handling.
- **The world does not guarantee the chosen people.** If the world contains them, the player starts among them. If not, the player starts anyway, possibly as the only one of their kin, and the game tells them so once the campaign starts.

Ownership split with the character epic (ep_01m4gbx49w72je0ezgjcfkxtjx, "DD2-quality character overhaul"): this epic owns the people registry, the creator's people list, generation timing, starts, the kin notice and the world's people identity. The character epic owns race bodies, heights, ears, skin colour, sliders (including Detailed Character Creation support) and each people's boons. The two meet at the people registry contract (people id → culture id, parent race id, presentation culture, race definition slot, boon set slot). This epic must not hard-code appearance or boon content. Until the character epic fills a slot, the selection shows that people with the installed human body and no boons, the creator audit reports the unfilled slot, and that state is not acceptance of the character epic's outcomes.

Known constraint to prove first: Sandbox registers campaign objects and the map before `CharacterCreationState`, and the current flow (MMR-43 world setup → generation → registration → creation limited to the presented cultures by MMR-32) generates before creation. Generating during creation needs a proven mechanism, for example hosting the creator before registration and applying its result afterwards, or deferring registration. An unsupported operation is a blocked gate with evidence, not a silent return to generate-first.

Unchanged from the FWGC epic: in-game generation only (no external tool, module publish or restart), save/world binding and War Sails. Future file and type names here are proposed implementation contracts. Saved in Backlog; no run is started.

successCriteria.text: In a generated campaign the character creator lists all 12 FWGC++ peoples as separate selections, whatever the generated world contains, each with its registry name, description and the boons and race body its people registry slots name. No vanilla culture entries are listed for generated campaigns; vanilla Sandbox character creation is unchanged.

World generation starts when the creator opens and runs during its stages. The creator stays responsive within a frame-time budget measured against the vanilla creator. If generation is still running at the last stage, the player sees progress and can cancel; cancel or a producer refusal returns to the setup screen with no partial campaign, temporary state or registered objects. No external tool, module publish or restart is involved.

If the world has the chosen people (at least one living hero or settlement of that civilization), the player starts at a navigable start in their lands by a documented rule. If not, the player starts at a documented deterministic fallback, and once the campaign starts a one-time in-game notice says they may be the only one of their kin. Both cases are tested on fixed seeds.

Generated realms, clans, heroes and notables of each people carry that people's culture identity, the same one the player can select, while troops, buildings, scenes and clothing still come from the presentation culture. The FWGC epic's campaign coherence (its s4) and naval behaviour (its s5) still pass.

Saves record the player's people, the world identity and whether the kin notice was shown. A cold load restores them without showing the notice again, and the FWGC epic's save binding (its s6) still holds.

A local one-shot run completes character creation for every one of the 12 peoples, including at least one fixed seed where the chosen people is present and one where it is absent, and records build, request, world and save identities plus generation and creator timings. Any observed correctness failure stays failed.

epic.title: FWGC++ peoples in the character creator, with world generation during creation

bundle.rationale:
Why two sprints: the core risk is the engine lifecycle. Sandbox registers the world before character creation today, so generating during creation is unproven. Sprint 1 traces the sequence, proves generation during an active creator and a 12-people list, and freezes the people registry; sprint 2 builds on the proven mechanism. If the proof picks a different mechanism, sprint 2 is re-planned at the sprint 1 checkpoint rather than built on a guess.

Parallelism: the trace and the people contract start together. The generation proof needs only the trace; the people-list proof needs both. In sprint 2, people registration, generation during creation and world identity can proceed in parallel; starts need generation and identity; saves need starts; the automated 12-people scenario joins everything.

Cross-epic boundary: the character epic (ep_01m4gbx49w72je0ezgjcfkxtjx) owns race bodies, heights, ears, skin colour, sliders, Detailed Character Creation support and boons, and fills the race and boon slots of the people registry. This epic can complete with unfilled slots shown as the documented fallback; that is not acceptance of the character epic.

User decisions recorded 2026-10-15: all 12 peoples are selections; the world does not guarantee the chosen people, and the player is told at campaign start when they may be the only one of their kin. The fallback start rule for an absent people was not specified by the user; the start ticket documents a deterministic rule and the sprint 2 checkpoint is where the user can change it.

No feature branch is created during planning. Execution setup records a codex/ feature branch before implementation and never merges to main directly.

tickets.body:
Write the people registry: one entry per FWGC++ civilization in `kEntityIds` at the producer.lock commit, in a fixed selection order. Each entry has the people id, display name and description (from `content_civilizations.cpp`), parent race id (read from FWGC++ civilization and heritage data, not guessed), presentation culture (`worldgen/policies/culture-presentations.json`), the culture StringId this epic registers (proposed `mnbl_people_<id>`), and two typed slots owned by the character epic: race definition and boon set. An unfilled slot resolves to a documented visible fallback (installed human body, no boons) and is reported, never silently defaulted. Add a schema and tests in C++ (next to the culture-presentation check in `campaign_semantics_tests.cpp`) and C# so drift from the generator registry or the presentation policy fails. Document the contract in `docs/peoples.md` as the interface the character epic consumes.

tickets.body:
Prove both halves before implementation. (1) The FWGC++ producer and WorldBridge compile run in the background while `CharacterCreationState` is active: progress reaches the creator, frame time is measured against the vanilla creator on the same settings, cancel works, and a producer refusal is surfaced. (2) The campaign side: the generated world is registered after the creator started, and the creator's result (people, appearance, narrative choices, banner, clan name) is applied to the generated campaign. Candidates include hosting the creator before world registration and replaying its result, or starting the campaign with registration deferred; choose by evidence from the sequence trace. Any engine operation that cannot be done is recorded as a blocked gate with the exact limiting API.
